in_text_mentions: The initial impression on the Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E) stained slides was a mucinous adenocarcinoma. The IHC disclosed the neoplastic cells to be positive for CK7 and GATA3 and negative for CK20, CDX2, and TTF1 (Figure 2). Based on the histopathological findings and the immunophenotype, two possibilities were considered; the first was a primary mucinous adenocarcinoma of the minor salivary glands, and the second was a metastatic adenocarcinoma, probably of breast origin. A guiding remark in the HPE report mentioned a thorough investigation of the primary site.
